Open questions

Everything the intelligence loop found that only a person may settle. Code detects and re-detects; nothing here resolves itself. An item that stops being detected LAPSES — lapsed is not settled, and a resolved item that is detected again reopens. Every card carries the full claim wording and the readings behind the detection, so it can be decided from this page alone.

Bars show the share of readings that landed the way the claim predicts. The two ticks are the detector's own gates: below 40% the evidence fails the claim, above 70% it supports it.

Resolve with RESOLVED_BY=<name> npm run intel:adjudicate -- --resolve <id> "reason"

1.00 majied (directed in chat 2026-09-04, executed by Claude) | corrected by Claude (analysis error found and corrected 2026-09-04; original text preserved) on 2026-09-04 (standing-flip): Acknowledged, and the ladder is working. Part of the cadence episode: see the decision recorded on the depth-vs-count items for the same claims (a690fa7e8570, 78ad45a6b0ee, e55dbd90d558), which carries the evidence. Short version: 24 of 87 channels held, the rejection stands on the count basis, and re-scoping is not available because the supporting side spans twelve niches. --- CORRECTION (2026-09-04, appended; the text above is kept as written): the figures '24 of 87 channels' and 'the supporting side spans twelve niches' are WRONG. They were computed by counting every observation row in the entry, which mixes lifetime-views rows with first-28-day rows; strengthObservations applies viewsBasisOf and grades one basis, because those are different quantities. On the basis the ladder actually uses, 58dd357134e4 grades 36 rows across 18 channels (held 39%) and 6bf44bfcf572 grades 53 rows across the same 18 (held 40%). Only TWO niches clear the stratum floor and they disagree sharply: maker-build held 63% (16 rows, 8 channels) against vlog-lifestyle 0% (6 rows, 3 channels); every other niche sits below the floor and carries no figure. So the conclusion drawn here was backwards. A re-scope WAS available, and on 2026-09-04 6bf44bfcf572, 58dd357134e4 and e377b6e6c637 were re-scoped to maker-build (RESCOPED_BY majied) and moved rejected -> candidate-law: the claim is true where the evidence supports it rather than demoted for failing to be true everywhere at once. The viewer-mix hypothesis recorded above rested on the same mixed count and should not be carried forward as stated; it needs recomputing on the graded basis before anyone pre-registers a test of it.

Depth vs count (4)

The ladder counts readings; these cards weigh them. Three bars per claim: the count the ladder judges on, the share of channels, and the share of VIDEOS behind the readings that held. When the depth reads a rejected claim as supported it is an un-rejection candidate; when it reads a promoted one as refuted it is an over-promotion candidate. Each side's niche make-up is named, because a claim carried by one niche is a demographic finding, not a general law.

One side of the evidence is mostly one niche. "When you stack a new upload within about a day and a half of your previous one, that burst…"

candidate-law

When you stack a new upload within about a day and a half of your previous one, that burst video tends to get roughly 25% fewer age-adjusted views than your typical non-burst upload — a pattern that held across 8 separate channels.

The question put to the data: On this channel, do uploads that arrived in a daily burst (within ~1.5 days of the previous upload) underperform the channel's non-burst baseline?

Why this fired: Flags: un-rejection = refuted-by-data but interval supports or video-weighted >= 60%; over-promotion = promoted at count >= 60% but interval refutes or video-weighted <= 40%; disagreement = video-weighted and count differ by >= 25 points; niche skew = one niche is >= 60% of a side and < 30% of the other. Nothing here moves a standing.

To resolve: Read the niche split; if one niche carries the claim, re-scope it or leave a note naming the demographic.

depth-vs-count0dbacaa5938b first 2026-09-02 · last 2026-09-05

A data-rejected claim the depth of evidence reads as SUPPORTED. "An audience's liking for a creative element follows an inverted-U against exposure count: …"

rejected

An audience's liking for a creative element follows an inverted-U against exposure count: it rises with repetition to a peak, then every further exposure reduces liking — so a format has a finite number of uses before it starts costing performance.

The question put to the data: Does a format wear out — do later episodes under-perform earlier ones?

Per-channel effects: mean +0.13, 95% interval 0.04 to 0.21 (k=15, normal approximation): supports. Supporting side by niche: maker-build 2, gaming 1, vlog-lifestyle 1, vanlife-travel 1; opposing: maker-build 5, motorcycle-travel 1, true-crime 1, vlog-lifestyle 2, homemaking 1.

Why this fired: Flags: un-rejection = refuted-by-data but interval supports or video-weighted >= 60%; over-promotion = promoted at count >= 60% but interval refutes or video-weighted <= 40%; disagreement = video-weighted and count differ by >= 25 points; niche skew = one niche is >= 60% of a side and < 30% of the other. Nothing here moves a standing.

To resolve: Either re-scope the claim to the niche carrying it (a niched claim is then graded in-niche), or record a note review. A data rejection reopens by itself when the count basis recovers; the depth view does not move it — that is your call.

Resolved by majied (directed in chat 2026-09-04, executed by Claude): Decided: the rejection STANDS and there is nothing to re-scope. 8 of 23 channels held, FOR median |effect| 0.26 against AGAINST median 0.07, so the depth view is picking up something real on a minority. But unlike the cadence family, NO recorded stratum separates the two sides: niche spread is 5pp (gaming 3/7 at 43%, maker-build 3/8 at 38%) and viewer-mix spread is 4pp (not-pulled 38%, discovery-driven 33%, mixed 33%). A depth-vs-count disagreement with no available moderator is not a scoping problem, it is an unexplained minority, and the honest record is that the claim is rejected on the evidence with the disagreement noted. Also flagged: this claim's evidence is byte-identical to f12d6e116bf7 (item 2a8675441478) — same channels, same effects — so the two are one arithmetic bound to two claims and should be counted once.

rejected

A repeated format decays: each additional instalment of the same idea loses remarkability until escalation is exhausted and views visibly plateau. Dream's Manhunt series is the named case.

The question put to the data: Does a format wear out — do later episodes under-perform earlier ones?

"Consistency of cadence matters more than the cadence itself. Whatever the interval, holdin" holds in true-crime and fails in restoration. Likely a niched truth wearing a general label.

candidate-law

Consistency of cadence matters more than the cadence itself. Whatever the interval, holding it reliably programs the audience to expect the next video; an erratic schedule costs more than a slow one. Frequency should then be set by niche: fast-moving interests (gaming, news) reward more frequent, lower-production uploads because timeliness is the value, while slower niches (homemaking, long-form build) can carry a monthly cadence when production quality is the value.

The question put to the data: On this channel, do uploads that arrived on the channel's usual rhythm out-perform ones that broke it?

stratum-proposal2b33b190ef27 first 2026-09-02 · last 2026-09-02

16 channels hold the same claims together (coherence 0.43) and no confirmed niche describes that set (closest: maker-build, overlap 0.47).

candidate-law

Longer videos do not reduce view counts: on a 30-video retention chart the longest-running curves were disproportionately the high-view ones, so length is not the constraint many creators assume.

lawsigned by majied

The first 30 seconds is the most important stretch of a long-form video: across our measured channels a median 35.1% of viewers are gone by 0:30 (middle half of channels 29.3-37.5%) and 44.7% by 1:00, so a fixed diagnostic pass belongs on the 0-60s window of every video.

candidate-law

Across 7 channels, longer runtimes tend to go with a smaller share of viewers still watching at the halfway mark, a moderate and consistent negative association.

candidate-law

Videos that hold more viewers through the first 30 seconds tend to also hold more viewers at the halfway mark, a mild positive association that showed up consistently across 9 channels.

Coherence rho(H) = mean over measured claims of |held ∩ H| / |held ∪ H| = 0.43 (floor 0.35). Channels: Mind Of A Criminal, Morley Kert, The BlackVeil Files, Jonny Builds, Kelly Hays, Emma Shaye, The Mountain Maker, Zac Builds, Studio NOHA, Tropical Russian, Man Made, Coffey Custom Builds, MoreNizarisaqt, Isabella Demarko, Visual Thinker, Her Two Wheels.

Why this fired: Greedy peel from every measured channel, keeping the best coherence at or above the floor within 60% of the fleet. Filed only when no confirmed niche covers 80% of the set. Re-filed only if coherence rises by 0.05.

To resolve: If these channels share something real (a format, an audience, a production model), confirm it as a niche on each; otherwise resolve with why the co-holding is coincidence.

stratum-proposal6529336d25ca first 2026-09-02 · last 2026-09-02

9 channels hold the same claims together (coherence 0.45) and no confirmed niche describes that set (closest: maker-build, overlap 0.46).

rejected

Consistency of cadence matters more than the cadence itself. Whatever the interval, holding it reliably programs the audience to expect the next video; an erratic schedule costs more than a slow one. Frequency should then be set by niche: fast-moving interests (gaming, news) reward more frequent, lower-production uploads because timeliness is the value, while slower niches (homemaking, long-form build) can carry a monthly cadence when production quality is the value.

candidate-law

Find a stable upload cadence and keep it, so the channel becomes part of viewers' weekly patterns; consistency of rhythm matters, not just raw frequency.

3 claims ride the same probe and direction (named-sponsor-opener-vs-ad-loss up) — one measurement counted 3 times. Merging is a human call; they may carry nuance the probe cannot see.

theory

The explicit sponsor callout phrase itself causes the drop, not the ad content: naming the sponsor up front is consistently followed by a retention decline, and disclosing AFTER demonstrating the product (framed as gratitude) avoids it.

theory

The phrase 'thanks to our sponsor' plus the brand name is itself the skip trigger; showing the product solving the problem FIRST and naming the sponsor only at the end of the segment reduces the drop.

theory

Saying the sponsor's name at the START of an integration is itself the trigger for the retention dip — it is an auditory cue that tells viewers exactly when to skip. Moving the words 'this video is sponsored by' to the END of the segment removes the cue.

The question put to the data: Do sponsor reads that open by naming the sponsor bleed more of the audience than reads that open some other way?

Why this fired: All 3 are graded by the SAME arithmetic in the same direction, so any "how many claims are measured" tally counts one test 3 times.

To resolve: Merge them into one claim (keeping the others as mergedFrom), or add a note naming the nuance that keeps them separate. Until then the honest measured-claims count subtracts the duplicates.

Resolved by majied: Merge directed in chat 2026-09-01, executed by Claude: kept b7150b575c17; nuance (remedy ordering, auditory-cue framing) recorded on the survivor's note.

2 claims ride the same probe and direction (retention-half-vs-views down) — one measurement counted 2 times. Merging is a human call; they may carry nuance the probe cannot see.

candidate-lawsigned by majied

Videos with more views systematically show LOWER average retention on the same channel, because wider reach pulls in newer, less-sticky viewers. A retention drop after a repackage is therefore not abnormal and is not by itself evidence the repackage failed — but it is not the desired outcome either: the aim is for retention to hold or improve as reach widens.

candidate-law

Within a channel, videos with the HIGHEST view counts systematically sit BELOW the channel's average retention, because wider reach pulls in newer, less sticky viewers — so falling retention on a breakout is expected, not a defect.

The question put to the data: Do the videos that hold viewers to halfway also get the most views?

Why this fired: All 2 are graded by the SAME arithmetic in the same direction, so any "how many claims are measured" tally counts one test 2 times.

To resolve: Merge them into one claim (keeping the others as mergedFrom), or add a note naming the nuance that keeps them separate. Until then the honest measured-claims count subtracts the duplicates.

Short version: 24 of 87 channels held, the rejection stands on the count basis, and re-scoping is not available because the supporting side spans twelve niches. --- CORRECTION (2026-09-04, appended; the text above is kept as written): the figures '24 of 87 channels' and 'the supporting side spans twelve niches' are WRONG. They were computed by counting every observation row in the entry, which mixes lifetime-views rows with first-28-day rows; strengthObservations applies viewsBasisOf and grades one basis, because those are different quantities. On the basis the ladder actually uses, 58dd357134e4 grades 36 rows across 18 channels (held 39%) and 6bf44bfcf572 grades 53 rows across the same 18 (held 40%). Only TWO niches clear the stratum floor and they disagree sharply: maker-build held 63% (16 rows, 8 channels) against vlog-lifestyle 0% (6 rows, 3 channels); every other niche sits below the floor and carries no figure. So the conclusion drawn here was backwards. A re-scope WAS available, and on 2026-09-04 6bf44bfcf572, 58dd357134e4 and e377b6e6c637 were re-scoped to maker-build (RESCOPED_BY majied) and moved rejected -> candidate-law: the claim is true where the evidence supports it rather than demoted for failing to be true everywhere at once. The viewer-mix hypothesis recorded above rested on the same mixed count and should not be carried forward as stated; it needs recomputing on the graded basis before anyone pre-registers a test of it.

stratum-proposal6c94f20986f3 first 2026-09-02 · last 2026-09-02

9 channels hold the same claims together (coherence 0.41) and no confirmed niche describes that set (closest: maker-build, overlap 0.38).

rejected

Consistency of cadence matters more than the cadence itself. Whatever the interval, holding it reliably programs the audience to expect the next video; an erratic schedule costs more than a slow one. Frequency should then be set by niche: fast-moving interests (gaming, news) reward more frequent, lower-production uploads because timeliness is the value, while slower niches (homemaking, long-form build) can carry a monthly cadence when production quality is the value.

candidate-law

Find a stable upload cadence and keep it, so the channel becomes part of viewers' weekly patterns; consistency of rhythm matters, not just raw frequency.

lawsigned by majied

The first 30 seconds is the most important stretch of a long-form video: across our measured channels a median 35.1% of viewers are gone by 0:30 (middle half of channels 29.3-37.5%) and 44.7% by 1:00, so a fixed diagnostic pass belongs on the 0-60s window of every video.

candidate-law

A near-duplicate of a proven format outperforms a wholly new one because familiarity does the work of removing risk while a small novel element supplies the reason to click — roughly a 90/10 split of template to twist.

Coherence rho(H) = mean over measured claims of |held ∩ H| / |held ∪ H| = 0.41 (floor 0.35). Channels: Mind Of A Criminal, Morley Kert, The BlackVeil Files, Jonny Builds, Zac Builds, Studio NOHA, Tropical Russian, Coffey Custom Builds, Her Two Wheels.

Why this fired: Greedy peel from every measured channel, keeping the best coherence at or above the floor within 60% of the fleet. Filed only when no confirmed niche covers 80% of the set. Re-filed only if coherence rises by 0.05.

To resolve: If these channels share something real (a format, an audience, a production model), confirm it as a niche on each; otherwise resolve with why the co-holding is coincidence.

Resolved by majied (directed in chat 2026-09-02, executed by Claude): Dismissed with reason: the nine channels are the curve-bearing, fully measured core of the fleet (coherence 0.41, nearest confirmed niche maker-build at 0.38, and the set spans maker, lifestyle and true-crime). Co-holding here reflects the general claims being measurable on the same well-covered channels, not a shared audience. Re-file if coherence rises by 0.05 or the set narrows to one niche's neighbours.

1.00 majied (directed in chat 2026-09-04, executed by Claude) on 2026-09-04 (standing-flip): Acknowledged, same cadence episode as 1eee6d6a4f93 and bba29fcb24c4. The move candidate-law -> rejected is the ladder doing its job on 24/87 channels held. The evidence and the reason re-scoping is unavailable are recorded on the depth-vs-count items for the same claims.

Per-channel effects: mean +0.21, 95% interval 0.08 to 0.33 (k=18, normal approximation): supports. Supporting side by niche: true-crime 2, maker-build 5; opposing: vlog-lifestyle 3, homemaking 1, maker-build 3, vanlife-travel 1, gaming 1, education 1, motorcycle-travel 1. maker-build is 71% of the supporting side and 27% of the other.

Why this fired: Flags: un-rejection = refuted-by-data but interval supports or video-weighted >= 60%; over-promotion = promoted at count >= 60% but interval refutes or video-weighted <= 40%; disagreement = video-weighted and count differ by >= 25 points; niche skew = one niche is >= 60% of a side and < 30% of the other. Nothing here moves a standing.

To resolve: Either re-scope the claim to the niche carrying it (a niched claim is then graded in-niche), or record a note review. A data rejection reopens by itself when the count basis recovers; the depth view does not move it — that is your call.

Resolved by majied (directed in chat 2026-09-04, executed by Claude) | corrected by Claude (analysis error found and corrected 2026-09-04; original text preserved): Decided: the data rejection STANDS on the count basis, and re-scoping to a niche is NOT available. Evidence, computed from the observation snapshots on 2026-09-04: 24 of 87 channels held, FOR median |effect| 0.38 against AGAINST median 0.10, so the depth view is right that the supporting side is carrying a real and much larger effect. But the queue's first remedy assumes ONE niche carries it, and the supporting side spans TWELVE: maker-build 6, commentary 4, beauty-fashion 2, true-crime 2, vlog-lifestyle 2, music 2, then climbing, vanlife-travel, product-review, home-renovation, gaming and one unstamped at 1 each. Hold rates do form a gradient (commentary 67%, maker-build 60%, down to restoration, homemaking and thrift-flip at 0%), but a gradient across twelve niches is not a niche that carries a claim, and scoping to any one of them would throw away five sixths of the supporting evidence. The most promising alternative moderator in the recorded strata is viewer mix among channels we have actually PULLED: discovery-driven 7/12 (58%) against mixed 0/6 (0%); 'not-pulled' is a sentinel covering 69 channels and forms no group. That is a HYPOTHESIS and is explicitly not being recorded as a finding: it comes from scanning four stratum axes post hoc over 18 channels, and the largest of four spreads is expected to look convincing by chance — the same multiple-comparison trap the packaging cross-check gates against. What would settle it: more channels with a classified viewer mix (today's 19 Studio pulls raise that population from a handful to 19), then a PRE-REGISTERED test of viewer mix alone rather than a scan. --- CORRECTION (2026-09-04, appended; the text above is kept as written): the figures '24 of 87 channels' and 'the supporting side spans twelve niches' are WRONG. They were computed by counting every observation row in the entry, which mixes lifetime-views rows with first-28-day rows; strengthObservations applies viewsBasisOf and grades one basis, because those are different quantities. On the basis the ladder actually uses, 58dd357134e4 grades 36 rows across 18 channels (held 39%) and 6bf44bfcf572 grades 53 rows across the same 18 (held 40%). Only TWO niches clear the stratum floor and they disagree sharply: maker-build held 63% (16 rows, 8 channels) against vlog-lifestyle 0% (6 rows, 3 channels); every other niche sits below the floor and carries no figure. So the conclusion drawn here was backwards. A re-scope WAS available, and on 2026-09-04 6bf44bfcf572, 58dd357134e4 and e377b6e6c637 were re-scoped to maker-build (RESCOPED_BY majied) and moved rejected -> candidate-law: the claim is true where the evidence supports it rather than demoted for failing to be true everywhere at once. The viewer-mix hypothesis recorded above rested on the same mixed count and should not be carried forward as stated; it needs recomputing on the graded basis before anyone pre-registers a test of it.

Resolved by majied (directed in chat 2026-09-04, executed by Claude) | corrected by Claude (analysis error found and corrected 2026-09-04; original text preserved): Same decision as a690fa7e8570. This is the third wording of the cadence claim and the third depth-vs-count item raised for one episode; all three share the same 87-channel evidence base. Resolving together so the queue stops showing one disagreement as three, and so a later reader is not misled into thinking three independent claims each failed. --- CORRECTION (2026-09-04, appended; the text above is kept as written): the figures '24 of 87 channels' and 'the supporting side spans twelve niches' are WRONG. They were computed by counting every observation row in the entry, which mixes lifetime-views rows with first-28-day rows; strengthObservations applies viewsBasisOf and grades one basis, because those are different quantities. On the basis the ladder actually uses, 58dd357134e4 grades 36 rows across 18 channels (held 39%) and 6bf44bfcf572 grades 53 rows across the same 18 (held 40%). Only TWO niches clear the stratum floor and they disagree sharply: maker-build held 63% (16 rows, 8 channels) against vlog-lifestyle 0% (6 rows, 3 channels); every other niche sits below the floor and carries no figure. So the conclusion drawn here was backwards. A re-scope WAS available, and on 2026-09-04 6bf44bfcf572, 58dd357134e4 and e377b6e6c637 were re-scoped to maker-build (RESCOPED_BY majied) and moved rejected -> candidate-law: the claim is true where the evidence supports it rather than demoted for failing to be true everywhere at once. The viewer-mix hypothesis recorded above rested on the same mixed count and should not be carried forward as stated; it needs recomputing on the graded basis before anyone pre-registers a test of it.
